newsitem.title: USA: Travelers Property Casualty returns to profitability.
newsitem.headline: Travelers Property Casualty returns to profitability.

text.p: Travelers Property Casualty Corp. posted a $276 million second-quarter profit Tuesday, a year after suffering a big loss related to its acquisition of Aetna's property casualty businesses.

The company reported a net income for the three months ended June 30 of $276.0 million, or 69 cents a share, compared with a loss of $216.2 million, or 59 cents a share in 1996, when it took $391 million in charges related to the acquisition and integration of the Aetna businesses.
Revenues for the quarter climbed to $2.43 billion from $2.20 billion.
Travelers also reported a 32 percent gain in operating earnings, which rose to $280.4 million, or 70 cents a share, from $213.0 million, or 56 cents a share.
"Earnings continued to climb as a result of strong net investment income, the low level of catastrophe losses, and continuing benefits from expense control," Chairman Robert Lipp said in a statement.

Lipp said the company achieved its goal, set last year, of $300 million in annualized expense savings ahead of schedule, and would continue to concentrate on reducing expenses as an important part of its operating philosophy.
"Those savings are critical to achieving a cost structure that enables us to remain competitive in the current marketplace," he said.
Lipp also said the company had begun to realise benefits from its investment in independent agents and other distribution channels for its auto and homeowners' policies.
Over the past year Travelers introduced new incentive programmes for its independent agents and an agent direct-mail marketing programme to support their businesses.
The company also said it recorded growth in other distribution channels, including Trevelers products sold through Primerica Financial Services and joint marketing arrangements with other insurers.
These channels currently account for about a third of the new policies written each month, the company said.
Travelers also said it spent about $241 million to buy back some 6.6 million shares of its stock from private investors.
The company also said its net written premiums for the quarter grew to $1.89 billion from $1.78 billion, excluding an adjustment associated with a reinsurance transaction.
For the first half of the year Travelers posted net income of $549.1 million, or $1.38 a share, compared with a net loss of $121.7 million, or 36 cents a share.
Revenues for the six months rose to $4.86 billion from $3.35 billion. Operating income almost doubled to $548.3 million, or $1.37 a share, from $293.8 million, or 87 cents a share.
Travelers stock lost 56 cents to $42.69 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
